rule: B is concrete depth, not vague enhancement. B31-B60 are subrequirements mapped to existing macro capabilities; they do not change the macro completion denominator unless a deduplication review proves a genuinely new independent product capability.

critical_research_corrections.statement: ConnectivityDiagnosticsManager registration success is not enough: Android invokes callbacks only for apps that offer connectivity, such as active VPNs, carrier apps with active subscriptions, or Wi-Fi suggesters; location permissions can also be required for location-bound networks.
critical_research_corrections.impact: 0.8 Lite Observer must not claim native data-stall diagnostics are active. Keep the adapter dormant until KINLINK qualifies, and continue using NetworkCallback/NetworkCapabilities/LinkProperties in Lite mode.

critical_research_corrections.statement: NetworkStatsManager cross-app/user-wide access requires user-granted Usage Access and queries can take seconds.
critical_research_corrections.impact: Make it optional, explicit and off the main thread; never make it a correctness dependency.

critical_research_corrections.statement: VpnService.Builder supports allowed/disallowed app rollout and explicit meteredness; VpnService can declare underlying networks.
critical_research_corrections.impact: Strong Stabilizer can be canary-deployed per app, preserve data-cost semantics and explicitly model underlying networks.

items.title: Diagnostics eligibility ladder
items.design: Separate universally available NetworkCallback/NetworkCapabilities/LinkProperties from ConnectivityDiagnostics callbacks that Android only delivers to eligible connectivity providers. Never call a silent registration success 'active diagnostics'.
items.acceptance: Lite Observer proves Tier 0; Tier 1 only when KINLINK itself qualifies as active VPN/carrier/Wi-Fi suggester and required permissions are explicit.

items.title: Probe budget and ambiguity resolver
items.design: Keep zero-probe observation as default. Allow only explicitly budgeted tiny active probes when passive evidence cannot distinguish WAN/DNS/remote-service failure; mobile probes default OFF.
items.acceptance: Every probe class has byte cap, transport policy, cooldown, user-visible rationale, privacy review and negative control.

items.title: Monotonic causal windows
items.design: Use wall time for human reports and monotonic elapsed time for durations, cooldowns, evidence windows and relapse logic.
items.acceptance: Clock changes cannot alter causal duration, cooldown or at-most-once reporting.

items.title: Privacy-preserving network identity
items.design: Represent trusted/home networks using pseudonymous local identifiers, confidence and recency; raw SSID/BSSID should not become general telemetry.
items.acceptance: Identity survives normal reconnects without exposing raw identifiers in exports; reset/forget is explicit.

items.title: Confidence calibration and abstention
items.design: Every diagnosis exposes evidence strength and can return UNKNOWN/HOLD rather than force a confident label.
items.acceptance: Calibration tests include false-positive/false-negative cases; UI never converts internal confidence into unsupported certainty.

items.title: Incident fingerprints and recurrence clustering
items.design: Create privacy-safe fingerprints for recurring combinations of transport, DNS, route, stall, handoff and resource symptoms.
items.acceptance: Clusters are reproducible from durable events and never rely on payload inspection.

items.title: Deterministic Personal Network Twin replay
items.design: Replay recorded event sequences through candidate policies offline before activation; compare candidate decisions with historical champion behavior.
items.acceptance: Same event trace + same policy version yields same decisions; replays cannot mutate production state.

items.title: Feature flags, kill switches and staged policy rollout
items.design: Every risky policy/action family gets a durable enablement flag, rollback target and blast-radius boundary.
items.acceptance: One switch can disable a harmful policy without reinstall; state is versioned and read back.

items.title: OEM survival qualification matrix
items.design: Qualify long-running observer behavior across Samsung/One UI and representative Android API levels, including reboot, idle, battery saver and process death.
items.acceptance: No OEM assumption is promoted from emulator-only evidence.

items.title: Existing VPN / Always-on / Lockdown coexistence
items.design: Detect incompatible VPN state and avoid breaking user networking. Strong Stabilizer must coexist or fail closed when another VPN/lockdown policy owns the path.
items.acceptance: Never silently replace an existing VPN; user escape path is always available.

items.title: Per-app canary rollout for Strong Stabilizer
items.design: Start with an allowlist of selected apps instead of whole-device interception to constrain blast radius.
items.acceptance: Allowed/disallowed sets are mutually exclusive, validated against installed packages and rollback to native networking.

items.title: TUN parser and data-plane fuzzing
items.design: Before any production VPN data plane, fuzz IPv4/IPv6/UDP/TCP/fragment/truncation/error paths and enforce memory bounds.
items.acceptance: Malformed packets cannot crash, loop, leak payloads or wedge teardown.

items.title: Transport migration awareness
items.design: Design future data plane so it does not break QUIC migration and can observe handoffs without inventing seamlessness it cannot guarantee.
items.acceptance: Tests cover address changes, NAT rebinding, path validation and rollback behavior.

items.title: Happy-Eyeballs strategy for KINLINK-owned connections
items.design: Where KINLINK itself opens diagnostic/control connections, prefer bounded IPv6/IPv4 racing rather than serial long stalls.
items.acceptance: Only KINLINK-owned sockets are affected; no claim of changing other apps without VPN/data plane.

items.title: Multi-path research gate, not a fake feature
items.design: Treat MPTCP/multi-path as a research/feasibility gate. Android app-space must not claim multipath aggregation unless the chosen stack and peers actually support it.
items.acceptance: Prototype must prove compatibility, cost, battery and server requirements before inclusion.

items.title: Meteredness inheritance contract
items.design: Future VPN must preserve or deliberately mark meteredness so downstream apps do not assume free data when underlying mobile is paid.
items.acceptance: Automated tests compare underlying and VPN metered state across Wi-Fi/mobile transitions.

items.title: Multi-SIM / subscription-aware policy
items.design: Model multiple mobile subscriptions separately where platform permission/role permits; never merge quotas or confidence across SIMs.
items.acceptance: Unknown subscription identity stays UNKNOWN; no subscriber identifiers are exported.

items.title: Resource SLO envelopes and percentile budgets
items.design: Move from single snapshots to rolling P50/P95 budgets for PSS, CPU, wakeups, battery drain and thermal throttling.
items.acceptance: Promotion fails if benefit is smaller than resource cost or if tail usage violates weak-device budgets.

items.title: Telemetry compaction and rebuildable indexes
items.design: Keep append-only canonical facts but compact/reindex derived views; indexes may be deleted and rebuilt from canonical events.
items.acceptance: Compaction never removes evidence required for active gates or unresolved incidents.

items.title: Diagnostic redaction and privacy classes
items.design: Assign privacy classes to every exported field and enforce allowlist-based diagnostic export.
items.acceptance: Secrets, raw payloads and unnecessary identifiers cannot enter export even after new modules are added.

items.title: Reproducible release metadata and SBOM
items.design: Record exact dependencies/toolchain/build provenance and generate a dependency inventory for every promoted artifact.
items.acceptance: A field artifact can be traced back to source commit, toolchain, signer and dependency set.

items.title: Backward-compatible telemetry/schema migration
items.design: Version every durable schema; migrations are idempotent, tested across skips and reversible where feasible.
items.acceptance: Old field data remains readable or has an explicit migration/tombstone path.

items.title: Capability discovery before policy activation
items.design: At runtime discover API level, permissions, VPN ownership, Usage Access, battery/thermal support and optional diagnostics eligibility before enabling features.
items.acceptance: UI and policy expose unavailable/optional/ready states instead of failing later.

items.title: Explainable action receipts
items.design: Every intervention should answer WHY, WHAT, EXPECTED BENEFIT, COST, RESULT and WHY NEXT/STOP in human and machine-readable forms.
items.acceptance: No action without durable receipt; UI can show concise human explanation without raw enum leakage.

items.title: Emergency disable and native-network escape
items.design: Provide a single local action to disable risky automation/data plane and return immediately to Android-native networking.
items.acceptance: Must work without Internet and without cloud/BCP availability.

items.title: Automatic harm rollback
items.design: If post-action evidence crosses harm thresholds, stop the policy, restore prior safe state and persist a harmful-outcome receipt.
items.acceptance: Rollback is bounded, idempotent and cannot oscillate indefinitely.

items.title: Network impairment replay lab
items.design: Turn recurring field failures into deterministic CI scenarios: flapping, latency, loss, DNS blackhole, WAN-down/LAN-up, captive, IPv6 partial, process kill and resource pressure.
items.acceptance: Each field incident can acquire a replay fixture and regression obligation.

items.title: Human-interaction budget
items.design: Treat taps, screenshots, reinstalls, permission trips and copy/paste as a measurable scarce resource, especially under fatigue/poor connectivity.
items.acceptance: A release plan states expected human actions and rejects avoidable repeated steps.

items.title: Bounded BCP diagnostic bridge
items.design: Expose signed, allowlisted, read-only diagnostic/receipt retrieval to the wider personal control plane before any remote actuation.
items.acceptance: No arbitrary shell, no secret export, local app remains correct if bridge is offline.

items.title: Dead-end / impossibility registry
items.design: Persist disproven approaches, platform restrictions and failed assumptions so future conversations do not rediscover the same dead end.
items.acceptance: Each entry records premise, evidence, scope, date, supersession condition and safe alternative.
